summary: Arakelov geometry needed for heights of abelian varieties, planned at target level for R35.1–R35.6 after the binding restructuring RS-06. R35.1 builds hermitian vector bundles over rings of integers, their Arakelov degree (independent of the section by the product formula, additive, multiplicative under base change), Arakelov divisors and the compactified Picard group, Gillet–Soulé arithmetic divisors with Green functions on regular flat (possibly non-proper, possibly S-localized) arithmetic schemes with ĈH¹ ≅ Pic^, the ℝ- or ℝ_S-valued pairing with proper 1-cycles (Zhang), the automorphism-weighted degree on relative dimension zero stacks (AGHMP), heights of points for continuous metrics and their identification with Mathlib's heights on projective space. R35.2 constructs the Hodge line of a smooth group scheme, the Faltings metric (with the corrected sign i^{g²}/2^g), its covolume form, behaviour under isogenies, products and duality, the metrized Hodge line over O_K, the hermitian pairing with the dual, the normalisation dictionary (Faltings, Deligne/Yuan–Zhang, unscaled/AGHMP/Tsimerman) and the elliptic period formula. R35.3 defines the Faltings height and the stable Faltings height, proves model, polarization and field independence, products and duality, and the lower bound for the bad-place correction. R35.4 proves the isogeny formula through Raynaud's different, the duality of differents, the ½ log deg bounds and denominators, the local terms along ℓ-divisible towers, and τ-component heights for O_E-actions. R35.5 treats metrics with logarithmic singularities, Northcott for them, the logarithmic growth of the Faltings metric, the Hodge-metrized modular line bundle on the minimal compactification, the identity h_mod = m·h_st, Northcott for the stable height, the theta height and Pazuki's comparison, and the elliptic bound h_st ≤ h(j)/12 + 3. R35.6 exports Zarhin's trick and its height identity, field-degree constants, finiteness of moduli points of bounded stable height, the lower bound for the Faltings height and the package consumed by FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems.

nodes.title: Hermitian vector bundles over the ring of integers
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field with ring of integers O_K and let Σ_K be the set of field embeddings σ : K → ℂ, on which complex conjugation acts by σ ↦ σ̄. A hermitian vector bundle Ē = (E, (h_σ)_{σ∈Σ_K}) over Spec O_K is a finitely generated projective O_K-module E together with, for every σ ∈ Σ_K, a positive definite hermitian inner product h_σ on the complex vector space E_σ = E ⊗_{O_K,σ} ℂ, such that h_{σ̄}(x ⊗ 1, y ⊗ 1) is the complex conjugate of h_σ(x ⊗ 1, y ⊗ 1) for all x, y ∈ E. Write ‖x‖_σ = h_σ(x, x)^{1/2}. The rank of Ē is the rank of E. A hermitian line bundle is a hermitian vector bundle of rank one. An isometry Ē ≅ F̄ is an O_K-linear isomorphism E ≅ F whose complexifications are unitary at every σ. Pic^(O_K) is the set of isometry classes of hermitian line bundles; it is an abelian group under the tensor product of the next node.
hypotheses: K a number field; E finitely generated and projective (equivalently torsion-free) over the Dedekind domain O_K.
The compatibility with complex conjugation is part of the data: at a real embedding it says h_σ is the complexification of a real inner product on E ⊗_σ ℝ.
Rank one is the case Faltings, Deligne and Szpiro call a metrized (compactified) invertible sheaf.
proofSteps: Define the structure from the module E, the family of inner products indexed by Σ_K, and the conjugation condition; for a rank-one bundle the data is equivalently one norm ‖·‖_v on E ⊗ K_v for each infinite place v (Deligne §1.1, p. 26; Szpiro §1.2, p. 13), which is how Mathlib's InfinitePlace records places.

Isometry classes form a set because E embeds in K^n and the inner products are finite-dimensional data; the group structure on Pic^(O_K) is the tensor product with inverse the dual (hermitian-operations).
acceptance: The trivial bundle Ō_K = (O_K, |·|_σ) is a hermitian line bundle; a fractional ideal 𝔞 with the restricted absolute values |σ(x)| is a hermitian line bundle; a hermitian line bundle whose metrics fail the conjugation condition is not an object of this definition.

sources.match: Defines a rank-one K-vector space with a v-adic absolute value at every place, the integral structure L_O giving the finite absolute values, and at each complex embedding a positive definite hermitian form with the conjugation compatibility; the real/complex normalisation of ‖·‖_v is fixed there.
Defines the compactified Picard group Pic_c(O_K): rank-one projective modules with positive definite hermitian forms at the infinite places, up to isometry.
Hermitian vector bundles over arithmetic schemes and over Spec O_K of arbitrary rank, their Arakelov degree and normalised degree, as used for slopes.

nodes.title: Sums, tensor products, duals, determinants, sub-bundles and base change
nodes.statement: For hermitian vector bundles Ē, F̄ over Spec O_K: (i) Ē ⊕ F̄ carries the orthogonal sum metric; (ii) Ē ⊗ F̄ = (E ⊗_{O_K} F, h^E_σ ⊗ h^F_σ); (iii) the dual Ē^∨ = (Hom(E, O_K), dual metric); (iv) the exterior powers Λ^k Ē with the induced metric, and the determinant det Ē = Λ^{rk E} Ē, a hermitian line bundle; (v) for an O_K-submodule F ⊂ E that is saturated (E/F torsion-free), F̄ carries the restricted metric and E/F the quotient metric (each h_σ on (E/F)_σ identified with the orthogonal complement of F_σ); (vi) for a finite extension L/K, the base change Ē_{O_L} = (E ⊗_{O_K} O_L, (h_{τ|K})_τ) with τ ∈ Σ_L extending σ = τ|_K. These are compatible with isometries and satisfy the usual identities: det(Ē ⊕ F̄) ≅ det Ē ⊗ det F̄, det(Ē^∨) ≅ (det Ē)^∨, and for 0 → F̄ → Ē → Q̄ → 0 with restricted and quotient metrics, det Ē ≅ det F̄ ⊗ det Q̄ isometrically.
hypotheses: F ⊂ E saturated, so that E/F is projective.
Base change uses that every τ ∈ Σ_L restricts to an element of Σ_K and every σ has exactly [L:K] extensions.
proofSteps: Form each module construction over O_K and the corresponding hermitian linear algebra fibrewise at each σ; the conjugation condition is preserved because every construction is natural.

For the determinant identity of an exact sequence choose at σ an orthonormal basis of F_σ completed by an orthonormal basis of its orthogonal complement, which maps isometrically onto Q_σ; the wedge of the combined basis has norm one, so the canonical isomorphism det E ≅ det F ⊗ det Q is an isometry (Deligne §2.1, p. 36, for the Hodge-line case).
Base change is functorial and compatible with ⊗, ∨ and det because these commute with the flat base change O_K → O_L.
acceptance: The identities are stated as isometries, not just module isomorphisms; Ō_K ⊗ Ē ≅ Ē; the dual of Ō_K is Ō_K.

nodes.title: The Arakelov degree of a hermitian bundle
nodes.statement: For a hermitian line bundle L̄ over Spec O_K and any nonzero s ∈ L, deg^(L̄) = log #(L / O_K·s) − Σ_{σ∈Σ_K} log ‖s‖_σ; equivalently, with Mathlib's infinite places and multiplicities mult(v) ∈ {1, 2}, deg^(L̄) = log #(L / O_K s) − Σ_v mult(v)·log ‖s‖_v. For a hermitian vector bundle, deg^(Ē) = deg^(det Ē), the normalised degree is deg^_n(Ē) = deg^(Ē)/[K:ℚ], and the slope is μ^(Ē) = deg^(Ē)/rank Ē. In Gillet–Soulé's normalisation an arithmetic divisor (Z, g) on Spec O_K has degree log #(Z) + ½ Σ_σ g_σ; the two agree through L̄ ↦ (div s, −log ‖s‖²).
hypotheses: L̄ a hermitian line bundle over Spec O_K (hermitian-vector-bundle).
#(L/O_K s) is the finite index of the submodule generated by s.
proofSteps: Define deg^ with a chosen nonzero section; independence of the choice is degree-independent-of-section, so deg^ is a function on Pic^(O_K).
For higher rank use the determinant of hermitian-operations; normalised degree and slope are quotients by [K:ℚ] and the rank.
acceptance: deg^(Ō_K) = 0; deg^ of a fractional ideal 𝔞 with the standard metric is −log N(𝔞); multiplying every metric by e^{−c} adds [K:ℚ]·c.

Grad(P) = log #(P/R·p) − Σ_v ε_v log ‖p‖_v with ε_v = 1, 2 at real and complex places.

nodes.title: Independence of the section: the product formula
nodes.statement: For a hermitian line bundle L̄ over Spec O_K and nonzero s, t ∈ L, log #(L/O_K s) − Σ_σ log ‖s‖_σ = log #(L/O_K t) − Σ_σ log ‖t‖_σ. Consequently deg^ : Pic^(O_K) → ℝ is a well-defined group homomorphism.
hypotheses: s, t ≠ 0 in L, so t = a s for a unique a ∈ K^×.
proofSteps: Write t = a·s with a ∈ K^×. The finite term changes by log #(L/O_K t) − log #(L/O_K s) = log |N_{K/ℚ}(a)| = −Σ_𝔭 log |a|_𝔭 (FractionalIdeal.absNorm_span_singleton).
The archimedean term changes by −Σ_σ log |σ(a)| = −log |N_{K/ℚ}(a)| (InfinitePlace.prod_eq_abs_norm).
The two changes cancel; this is the product formula NumberField.prod_abs_eq_one. Additivity under ⊗ follows by taking s ⊗ s′ as the section of L ⊗ L′ (degree-additivity).
acceptance: Replacing s by 2s in Ō_ℚ leaves log 2 − log 2 = 0; for K = ℚ(√2) and a = 1 + √2 a unit, both terms are unchanged separately.

sources.match: By the product formula ∏_v ‖λℓ‖_v = ∏_v ‖ℓ‖_v for λ ∈ K^×, so the degree does not depend on ℓ.
Grad is independent of the section p by the product formula.
The map from compactified divisors to Pic_c is an isomorphism modulo principal divisors; principal divisors have degree zero by the product formula.

nodes.title: Additivity of the Arakelov degree
nodes.statement: For hermitian vector bundles over Spec O_K: deg^(L̄ ⊗ M̄) = deg^(L̄) + deg^(M̄) and deg^(L̄^∨) = −deg^(L̄) for line bundles; deg^(Ē ⊕ F̄) = deg^(Ē) + deg^(F̄); for an exact sequence 0 → F̄ → Ē → Q̄ → 0 with restricted and quotient metrics, deg^(Ē) = deg^(F̄) + deg^(Q̄). If L ⊂ L′ are hermitian line bundles with the same generic fibre and the same metrics, deg^(L̄′) = deg^(L̄) + log #(L′/L).
hypotheses: The sub-bundle F is saturated in E.
In the last statement L and L′ are O_K-lattices in one K-line with equal metrics at every σ.
proofSteps: For tensor products use the section s ⊗ s′: the index is multiplicative, #(L ⊗ M / O_K(s ⊗ s′)) = #(L/O_K s)·#(M/O_K s′), and norms multiply.
Dual: pair s with the dual section s^∨ with s^∨(s) = 1 on L ⊗ K; ‖s^∨‖_σ = ‖s‖_σ^{−1}, and the index of O_K s^∨ in L^∨ equals that of O_K s in L.

nodes.title: Arakelov divisors on Spec O_K and the compactified Picard group
nodes.statement: The group Div^(O_K) of Arakelov divisors is the set of formal sums D = Σ_𝔭 n_𝔭[𝔭] + Σ_v λ_v[v] with n_𝔭 ∈ ℤ almost all zero (𝔭 nonzero primes) and λ_v ∈ ℝ (v infinite places); its degree is deg^(D) = Σ_𝔭 n_𝔭 log N𝔭 + Σ_v λ_v. The principal divisor of f ∈ K^× is (f) = Σ_𝔭 ord_𝔭(f)[𝔭] − Σ_v mult(v)·log|f|_v [v]. The map D ↦ O(D) = (𝔞_D^{-1}, ‖x‖_v = e^{−λ_v/mult(v)}|x|_v), 𝔞_D = ∏𝔭^{n_𝔭}, induces an isomorphism Div^(O_K)/{principal} ≅ Pic^(O_K) carrying deg^ to the Arakelov degree, and there is an exact sequence 0 → ℝ^{r_1 + r_2}/log|O_K^×| → Pic^(O_K) → Cl(K) → 0, where log|O_K^×| is the image of the units under u ↦ (mult(v) log|u|_v)_v. In Gillet–Soulé's language Div^(O_K)/principal is ĈH¹(Spec O_K) with Green functions g_v = 2λ_v/mult(v).
hypotheses: K a number field; r_1, r_2 the numbers of real and complex places.
proofSteps: Define D ↦ O(D) and check that (f) ↦ the trivial bundle with the section f, using ‖f‖_v = 1 after twisting (Szpiro, Proposition 1.1).
Surjectivity: a hermitian line bundle L̄ with a section s ≠ 0 is O(D) for D = Ψ(L̄, s) = Σ ord_𝔭(𝔞_s)[𝔭] − Σ_v mult(v) log ‖s‖_v [v]; changing s changes D by a principal divisor.
Degree compatibility is the definition of arithmetic-degree; principal divisors have degree zero (degree-independent-of-section).
The exact sequence: the kernel of Pic^(O_K) → Cl(K) is represented by divisors supported at infinity, modulo the principal divisors of units (Gillet–Soulé §3.4.3).
acceptance: deg^((f)) = 0 for every f ∈ K^×; for K = ℚ, Pic^(ℤ) ≅ ℝ through deg^.

nodes.title: Arithmetic divisors with Green functions and ĈH¹
nodes.statement: Let X be a regular scheme, flat, separated and of finite type over B = Spec O_K or over B_S = Spec O_K ∖ S for a finite set S of nonzero primes, with smooth generic fibre; X need not be proper. For σ ∈ Σ_K write X_σ(ℂ) for the complex manifold of X ⊗_σ ℂ, and F_∞ for complex conjugation acting on ⊔_σ X_σ(ℂ). An arithmetic divisor is a pair D̂ = (D, g) with D a Cartier divisor on X (ℚ-coefficients allowed) and g = (g_σ) a Green function for D: g_σ is a smooth real function on X_σ(ℂ) ∖ D_σ(ℂ), F_∞-invariant across σ, such that for every local equation f of D the function g_σ + log|f|² extends smoothly. Div^(X) is the group of arithmetic divisors; the principal arithmetic divisor of a rational function f ≠ 0 is d̂iv(f) = (div f, (−log|f|²_σ)_σ); ĈH¹(X) = Div^(X)/{principal}. The classes supported over S, ĈH¹_{|S|}(X), are those (D, 0) with D supported in fibres over primes of S; for X over O_K and X_S = X ×_B B_S restriction induces ĈH¹(X)/ĈH¹_{|S|}(X) ≅ ĈH¹(X_S).
hypotheses: X regular, flat and separated of finite type over B or B_S, with smooth generic fibre; Cartier divisors and Weil divisors agree on the regular X (SF.3).
Green functions are smooth Green currents of logarithmic type in Gillet–Soulé's sense for divisors; no log-log growth is allowed in this node.
ℚ-coefficients: ĈH¹(X)_ℚ = ĈH¹(X) ⊗ ℚ is the group used by Zhang's localized pairing.
proofSteps: Define Div^(X) as pairs; principal divisors are arithmetic divisors because −log|f|² + log|f|² = 0 extends trivially (Poincaré–Lelong: dd^c of −log|f|² is the current of div f).
ĈH¹(X) is the quotient; on Spec O_K it is the group of arakelov-divisors-of-number-field (g_v = 2λ_v/mult(v)).

Localization: an element of ĈH¹(X) restricts to X_S; its kernel is generated by vertical divisors over S together with their principal relations, which is ĈH¹_{|S|}(X) (Zhang, Remark 8.5). For B = Spec ℤ and a prime p the vertical fibre V_p satisfies (V_p, 0) = (0, 2 log p) in ĈH¹(X), since d̂iv(p) = (V_p, −2 log p).
acceptance: The relation (V_p, 0) ≡ (0, 2 log p) over ℤ; on Spec O_K the definition recovers Szpiro's compactified divisors.

nodes.title: Metrized line bundles and arithmetic divisors
nodes.statement: For X as in arithmetic-divisors-green, let Pic^(X) be the group of isometry classes of line bundles on X with an F_∞-invariant smooth hermitian metric on L_ℂ over ⊔_σ X_σ(ℂ). The map ĉ₁ : Pic^(X) → ĈH¹(X), L̄ ↦ (div s, −log ‖s‖²) for any nonzero rational section s, is a well-defined group isomorphism. For a morphism f : X′ → X of such schemes with f(X′) not contained in the support, ĉ₁(f^*L̄) = f^*ĉ₁(L̄).
hypotheses: X regular, so Cartier divisors and line bundles with rational sections correspond.
Metrics are smooth and F_∞-invariant.
proofSteps: Changing s to fs changes (div s, −log‖s‖²) by d̂iv(f), so the class is independent of s.
−log ‖s‖² is a Green function for div s: locally s = u·f·e with e a frame, so −log‖s‖² + log|f|² = −log(|u|²‖e‖²) is smooth.
Inverse: from (D, g) form O(D) with the metric ‖1_D‖² = e^{−g}; isometry classes correspond to classes modulo principal divisors.
Group laws: ⊗ goes to + since ‖s ⊗ t‖ = ‖s‖‖t‖. Pullback compatibility follows from the formulas.
acceptance: On Spec O_K this is the isomorphism of arakelov-divisors-of-number-field; for X = Spec ℤ, ĉ₁(ℤ, r|·|) = (0, −2 log r) of degree −log r.

nodes.title: Arithmetic degree of ĈH¹ on proper one-cycles
nodes.statement: Let X be regular and flat over B = Spec O_K (or B_S) with smooth generic fibre, and Z_1^c(X) the group of 1-cycles on X proper over the base. There is a bilinear pairing (·,·) : ĈH¹(X)_ℚ × Z_1^c(X)_ℚ → ℝ (respectively ℝ_S = ℝ/span_ℚ{log p : some prime of S lies over p} over B_S), defined on an irreducible C not contained in |D| as follows: if C is horizontal with normalization ν : Spec O_{K(C)} → X, (D̂, C) = deg^(ν^*ĉ₁^{-1}(D̂)), the Arakelov degree of the pulled-back hermitian line bundle over O_{K(C)}, equivalently Σ_{x ∈ C ∩ |D|} i_x(C, D)·log #k(x) + ½ Σ_{y ∈ C(ℂ)} g(y), where i_x(C, D) is the length at x of the restriction of D to the normalization of C; if C is vertical, lying in the fibre over 𝔭, (D̂, C) = deg_{C}(O(D)|_C)·log N𝔭. The value depends only on the class of D̂, extends to all C by moving D̂ within its class, and on vertical cycles depends only on rational equivalence inside proper subschemes of special fibres; this defines the pairing on the quotient Z_1(X) of Z_1^c(X) by such cycles. The height of a point x ∈ X(K′) with closure C_x is h_{D̂}(x) = (D̂, C_x)/[K′:ℚ] when X is proper.
hypotheses: Horizontal 1-cycles proper over the base are finite over it, so their normalizations are spectra of rings of integers.
Over B_S the finite contributions at primes of S are not defined, so values are taken modulo ℚ-multiples of their logarithms.
proofSteps: Horizontal case: ν^*O(D) with the pulled-back metric is a hermitian line bundle over O_{K(C)}; its degree splits into the finite intersection multiplicities with D and the archimedean values of g at the points of C(ℂ).

Independence of the class: a principal divisor d̂iv(f) pairs to deg^ of a principal divisor on O_{K(C)}, which is 0 (degree-independent-of-section), and vertical principal relations pair to 0 by the degree of a principal divisor on a proper curve over a field.
Over B_S the finite contributions at S are only defined up to ℚ·log p, giving values in ℝ_S; Zhang (9.3) applies the same definition with the base Spec O_E ∖ S.
Extension to curves inside |D| uses moving lemmas on regular X (Bost–Gillet–Soulé §2.3, as cited by Zhang).
acceptance: Over Spec ℤ, (0, 2 log p) pairs with the horizontal section of ℙ¹_ℤ to log p, matching ([p], 0); inverting a new prime p enlarges the quotient ℝ_S by ℚ log p.

nodes.title: Arithmetic degree on relative dimension zero Deligne–Mumford stacks
nodes.statement: Let Y be a Deligne–Mumford stack, flat, proper and quasi-finite (relative dimension 0) over Spec O_E, with finite inertia. ĈH¹(Y) is the group of pairs (Z, Φ) with Z a Cartier divisor (supported in positive characteristic) and Φ an F_∞-invariant real function on Y(ℂ), modulo d̂iv(Ψ) = (div Ψ, −log|Ψ|²), and Pic^(Y) ≅ ĈH¹(Y). Its arithmetic degree is the homomorphism deg^ : ĈH¹(Y) → ℝ with deg^(Z, 0) = Σ_𝔮 log N(𝔮)·Σ_{z ∈ Z(F̄_𝔮)} length(O^{et}_{Z,z})/#Aut(z) for Z effective, and deg^(0, Φ) = ½ Σ_{y ∈ Y(ℂ)} Φ(y)/#Aut(y). For a finite étale morphism Y′ → Y of degree d, deg^(π^*D̂) = d·deg^(D̂); for Y = Spec O_L it is the Arakelov degree over O_L.
hypotheses: Y finite flat over O_E as a stack: every geometric point has finite automorphism group.
O^{et}_{Z,z} is the étale local ring at z; residue-field norms N(𝔮), not the residue characteristic, weight each prime.
proofSteps: Define the degree on effective divisors and on Green functions by the displayed weighted sums; principal divisors have degree zero by the product formula applied on an étale atlas by schemes and division by automorphism orders.
Pic^(Y) ≅ ĈH¹(Y) is the stack version of pic-hat-iso-chow-hat, glued by étale descent (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.3).
Finite étale pullback: each geometric point of Y has d preimages counted with automorphism weights, so both sums scale by d.
For a scheme Y = Spec O_L every automorphism group is trivial and the formula is deg^ of arithmetic-degree.

nodes.title: Heights of algebraic points for metrized line bundles
nodes.statement: Let 𝒳 be a projective flat scheme over Spec ℤ (or over Spec O_K), X = 𝒳_ℚ, ℒ a line bundle on 𝒳 and ‖·‖ a continuous F_∞-invariant hermitian metric on ℒ_ℂ over 𝒳(ℂ). For a number field K′ and x ∈ X(K′), let x̄ : Spec O_{K′} → 𝒳 extend x (properness) and set h_{ℒ̄}(x) = deg^(x̄^*ℒ, x^*‖·‖)/[K′:ℚ]. This depends only on the image of x in X(ℚ̄), giving h_{ℒ̄} : X(ℚ̄) → ℝ. Changing the integral model of (X, L) changes h by a bounded function; changing the continuous metric by φ = log(‖·‖′/‖·‖) changes h by at most sup|φ|.
hypotheses: 𝒳 proper over the base, so every K′-point extends uniquely to O_{K′}.
Metrics are continuous (not necessarily smooth); smooth metrics give the pairing of arithmetic-degree-pairing on the closure of x.
proofSteps: Existence and uniqueness of x̄ is the valuative criterion of properness; x̄^*ℒ with x^*‖·‖ is a hermitian line bundle over O_{K′}.

nodes.title: Metrized heights represent Weil heights; Northcott for ample bundles
nodes.statement: In the situation of heights-of-points, h_{ℒ̄} represents the Weil height class h_{L} of RP.0's height machine for the generic fibre (X, L): h_{ℒ̄} − h_L is bounded on X(ℚ̄). nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, n ≥ 0 and x = (x_0, …, x_n) ∈ K^{n+1} ∖ {0} with point [x] ∈ ℙⁿ(K). Let 𝔟 ⊂ K be the fractional ideal generated by the coordinates. The hermitian line bundle x̄^*O(1) with the sup metric (‖ℓ‖_σ = |ℓ(x)|_σ / max_i |x_i|_σ for linear forms ℓ) is isometric to O(D_x) for the Arakelov divisor D_x = (𝔟^{-1}, v ↦ mult(v)·log max_i |x_i|_v), and deg^(x̄^*Ō(1)_sup) = log N(𝔟^{-1}) + Σ_v mult(v) log max_i |x_i|_v = Height.logHeight x, the logarithm of Mathlib's relative multiplicative height of the tuple; it depends only on [x] and equals Projectivization.logHeight [x]. With the Fubini–Study metric ‖ℓ‖_σ = |ℓ(x)|_σ/(Σ_i |x_i|²_σ)^{1/2} the degree is log of the Arakelov (ℓ²) height, and 0 ≤ deg^_FS − deg^_sup ≤ ½[K:ℚ]·log(n + 1).

nodes.title: Hermitian ℚ-lines and norms of hermitian line bundles
nodes.statement: (a) The group of hermitian ℚ-line bundles over Spec O_K is Pic^(O_K)_ℚ = Pic^(O_K) ⊗ ℚ, with deg^ extended ℚ-linearly; equivalently ĈH¹(Spec O_K)_ℚ. (b) For a finite extension L/K, the norm N_{L/K} : Pic^(O_L) → Pic^(O_K) sends M̄ = (M, ‖·‖) to the norm N_{O_L/O_K}(M) of the invertible O_L-module with the metrics ‖N(m)‖_σ = ∏_{τ ∈ Σ_L, τ|_K = σ} ‖m‖_τ; it is a group homomorphism, corresponds to the push-forward ĈH¹(Spec O_L) → ĈH¹(Spec O_K), and satisfies deg^(N_{L/K} M̄) = deg^(M̄) and N_{L/K}(L̄_{O_L}) ≅ L̄^{⊗[L:K]} for L̄ over O_K. (c) For a finite étale (or finite flat) morphism of arithmetic schemes the norm of metrized line bundles is defined the same way fibrewise and is compatible with heights: h_{N_{Y/X} M̄}(x) is the sum of h_{M̄} over the points above x, divided appropriately by degrees.

proofSteps: (a) Tensor with ℚ; deg^ is a homomorphism (degree-additivity).

(b) The norm of an invertible O_L-module along the finite flat O_K → O_L exists and is multiplicative (SF.3 line-bundle-norm); for m ∈ M nonzero, N(m) generates a submodule of index #(M/O_L m), since the absolute norm is transitive; the archimedean norms multiply over the [L:K] embeddings above each σ, so deg^ is preserved.

nodes.title: The Hodge line of a smooth commutative group scheme
nodes.statement: Let S be a scheme and G → S a smooth separated commutative group scheme of finite presentation, of constant relative dimension g, with unit section e. Its Hodge bundle is ω_G = e^*Ω¹_{G/S} = Lie(G/S)^∨, locally free of rank g, and its Hodge line is ω̄_G := det ω_G = e^*Ω^g_{G/S} = Λ^g Lie(G/S)^∨. (a) Formation of ω_G and of its determinant commutes with every base change S′ → S. (b) For an open subgroup scheme G⁰ ⊂ G containing e(S) (for instance the fibrewise identity component of a Néron model) restriction is an isomorphism ω̄_G = ω̄_{G⁰}. (c) A homomorphism φ : G → H of such group schemes of the same relative dimension induces φ^* : ω̄_H → ω̄_G; ω̄_{G×H} ≅ ω̄_G ⊗ ω̄_H. (d) If G → S is proper (an abelian scheme), evaluation at e gives p_*Ω^g_{G/S} ≅ ω̄_G and agrees with the Hodge line of AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A6; without properness p_*Ω^g need not be ω̄_G.
hypotheses: G smooth, separated, commutative, finitely presented over S, all fibres of dimension g.
In (d) the comparison is for abelian schemes; for a semi-abelian scheme only the definition e^*Ω^g is used.
proofSteps: ω_G = e^*Ω¹_{G/S} is locally free of rank g because G is smooth of relative dimension g; Ω¹_{G/S} ≅ p^*ω_G by translation invariance, so Ω^g_{G/S} ≅ p^*ω̄_G and e^*Ω^g = ω̄_G.
Base change: Ω¹ commutes with base change and pullback along e commutes with base change.
(b) is local at e(S); (c) pulls back differentials along φ and uses Ω¹_{G×H} = pr_1^*Ω¹_G ⊕ pr_2^*Ω¹_H.
(d) For an abelian scheme p_*O_G = O_S universally, so p_*Ω^g = p_*p^*ω̄_G = ω̄_G (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A1 relative-invariant-forms).
acceptance: For G = 𝔾_m over Spec ℤ, ω̄_G = ℤ·dt/t; p_*Ω¹ = ℤ[t, t^{-1}]·dt/t is not of rank one, which is why (d) needs properness.

nodes.title: The Faltings metric on top differential forms
nodes.statement: For a complex abelian variety A of dimension g, the one-dimensional space H⁰(A, Ω^g) carries the hermitian form ⟨α, β⟩_Fal = (i^{g²}/2^g)·∫_{A(ℂ)} α ∧ β̄. It is positive definite: ‖α‖²_Fal = 2^{−g}·|∫_{A(ℂ)} α ∧ ᾱ| > 0 for α ≠ 0, and i^{g²} ∫ α ∧ ᾱ is a positive real number, i^{g²} = i^g(−1)^{g(g−1)/2}. Other normalisations in use are ‖α‖²_Del = (2π)^{−g}|∫ α ∧ ᾱ| (Deligne, Bost, Yuan–Zhang, Gaudron–Rémond) and ‖α‖²_un = |∫ α ∧ ᾱ| (Tsimerman, Andreatta–Goren–Howard–Madapusi Pera); see normalization-adapter.
hypotheses: A a complex abelian variety (compact complex torus with a polarization) of dimension g ≥ 0; for g = 0, H⁰ = ℂ with ‖1‖ = 1.
Faltings prints (i/2)^g ∫ α ∧ ᾱ, which is negative for g ≡ 2, 3 mod 4; the factor i^{g²} = i^g(−1)^{g(g−1)/2} corrects the sign (source issue E1).
proofSteps: In linear coordinates z_1, …, z_g on A(ℂ) = ℂ^g/Λ write α = c·dz_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ dz_g. Then α ∧ ᾱ = |c|²(−1)^{g(g−1)/2}∏_j(dz_j ∧ dz̄_j) and dz_j ∧ dz̄_j = −2i dx_j ∧ dy_j.
Hence (i^{g²}/2^g)α ∧ ᾱ = |c|²·dx_1 ∧ dy_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ dx_g ∧ dy_g, the Lebesgue volume form; integrating gives |c|²·vol(ℂ^g/Λ) > 0 (covolume-formula).
Sesquilinearity and hermitian symmetry follow from conjugating the integrand; the form is invariant under all automorphisms of A since they preserve ∫.

nodes.title: The Faltings norm is a covolume
nodes.statement: Let A(ℂ) ≅ V/Λ with V = T₀A ≅ ℂ^g and Λ the period lattice (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A5). For a basis z_1, …, z_g of linear coordinates on V, ‖dz_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ dz_g‖²_Fal = covol(Λ), the Lebesgue covolume of Λ in ℂ^g = ℝ^{2g}. In the Siegel normalisation Λ = ℤ^g + τℤ^g with τ ∈ ℍ_g, ‖dz_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ dz_g‖²_Fal = det(Im τ); for a general basis of periods (Ω_1 | Ω_2) with Ω_1 invertible and τ = Ω_1^{−1}Ω_2, the form dual to the basis has squared norm |det Ω_1|²·det(Im τ). For g = 1 and Λ = ℤω_1 + ℤω_2 with Im(ω_2/ω_1) > 0, ‖dz‖²_Fal = |ω_1|²·Im(ω_2/ω_1) = area of ℂ/Λ.

nodes.title: The metrized Hodge line bundle over O_K
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field and G → Spec O_K a smooth separated commutative group scheme of finite type whose generic fibre A = G_K is an abelian variety of dimension g (a Néron model, its identity component, or a semi-abelian model). The metrized Hodge line ω̄̂(G) is the hermitian line bundle over Spec O_K whose module is ω̄_G (hodge-line-of-group-scheme) and whose metric at σ ∈ Σ_K is the Faltings metric on ω̄_G ⊗_σ ℂ = H⁰(A_σ, Ω^g), A_σ = A ⊗_{K,σ} ℂ. The archimedean data depend only on A; the finite data depend on the model, and for the Néron model 𝒜 of A one writes ω̄̂(A/K) = ω̄̂(𝒜) = ω̄̂(𝒜⁰). For a finite extension L/K there is a canonical injection ω̄_{𝒜} ⊗_{O_K} O_L ⊇ ω̄_{𝒜_L} of lattices in ω̄(A_L) (the pullback along 𝒜 ⊗ O_L → 𝒜_L from the Néron mapping property) which is an isometry at every complex embedding.
hypotheses: G smooth over O_K with abelian generic fibre; the Néron model exists by NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.1.
The conjugation condition holds because A_{σ̄} is the complex conjugate variety of A_σ and the Faltings form is conjugation-compatible.
proofSteps: Module: ω̄_G is a projective O_K-module of rank one (hodge-line-of-group-scheme, R11.1 differential-lattice); its generic fibre is H⁰(A, Ω^g).
Metric: faltings-hermitian-form at each σ; conjugation compatibility from faltings-hermitian-form's conjugation API.

Base change map: the Néron mapping property gives 𝒜 ⊗_{O_K} O_L → 𝒜_L extending the identity; pulling back invariant differentials gives ω̄_{𝒜_L} → ω̄_{𝒜} ⊗ O_L, injective because it is the identity on generic fibres; the archimedean metrics are computed on the same complex abelian varieties.
acceptance: For A = E an elliptic curve over ℚ with Néron differential ω_N, ω̄̂(E/ℚ) = (ℤ·ω_N, ‖ω_N‖² = area of ℂ/Λ_{ω_N}); LMFDB's Faltings height of 11.a2 is −½ log of that area, −0.30801…

nodes.title: The Hodge lines of A and its dual
nodes.statement: Let A be an abelian variety over a number field K with dual A^t. (a) (Raynaud) For the Néron models 𝒜, 𝒜′ of A and A^t, the metrized Hodge lines satisfy ω̄̂(𝒜)^{⊗2} ≅ ω̄̂(𝒜′)^{⊗2} isometrically; in particular deg^ ω̄̂(A/K) = deg^ ω̄̂(A^t/K). (b) (Faltings–Chai) If A has semistable reduction over K, so that the Néron identity components 𝒢 of A and 𝒢^t of A^t are semi-abelian, there is a natural isomorphism ω̄_𝒢 ≅ ω̄_{𝒢^t} extending the Serre-duality isomorphism on the generic fibre, and it is an isometry for the Faltings metrics. For an isogeny α : G → G₁ with dual α^t, the comparison maps p satisfy deg(α)·p_{G₁} = α^{t*} ∘ p_G ∘ α^*.
hypotheses: (a) holds for arbitrary Néron models (semistability not needed).
(b) S normal, G semi-abelian, abelian over a dense open of S.
proofSteps: (a) Choose an ample line bundle and its polarization u_K : A → A^t of degree d. By Raynaud's Theorem 2.1.1 the differents of u and of its dual satisfy 𝔡_u 𝔡_{u′} = (d); as u is self-dual this gives 𝔡_u² = (d), so 1/d trivializes ω_u^{⊗2} with its metrics (isogeny-pullback-norm gives the archimedean norm d), whence ω̄̂(𝒜)^{⊗2} ≅ ω̄̂(𝒜′)^{⊗2}.

(b) Over the abelian locus Serre duality identifies ω_G with the dual of R^g f_*O_G = det(R¹f_*O_G), which is dual to ω_{G^t}; the isomorphism extends over codimension one by a degeneration computation with Mumford's construction over a complete DVR, using the isogeny formula to compare the orders of pole at the boundary.
Isometry over ℂ: the polarization identifies H⁰(A, Ω^g) with H⁰(A^t, Ω^g) and the Riemann form computes both volumes.
acceptance: For an elliptic curve E, A^t ≅ A and both statements are tautological; for a principally polarized A the canonical isomorphism ω̄_A ≅ ω̄_{A^t} is induced by the polarization.

nodes.title: Normalisations of the Faltings metric and height
nodes.statement: For an abelian variety A of dimension g over a number field and any model, the three metrics on the Hodge line satisfy ‖α‖²_Del = π^{−g}‖α‖²_Fal and ‖α‖²_un = 2^g‖α‖²_Fal, so the normalised degrees h_• = deg^/[K:ℚ] satisfy h_Del = h_Fal + (g/2) log π and h_un = h_Fal − (g/2) log 2 = h_Del − (g/2) log(2π). Thus Yuan–Zhang's and Gaudron–Rémond's h(A) is h_Del; Faltings' original height (also Bilu–Parent–Rebolledo's h_F) is h_Fal; Tsimerman's and Andreatta–Goren–Howard–Madapusi Pera's h_Falt, and Colmez's, is h_un; in particular h_YZ = h_AGHMP + (g/2) log(2π). More generally multiplying every squared norm by c > 0 changes the normalised height by −½ log c, and the finite lattices are unchanged.
hypotheses: The same model and the same finite lattice are used on both sides; only the archimedean metrics differ.
proofSteps: Multiplying ‖·‖²_σ by c at every σ subtracts ½ Σ_σ log c = ½[K:ℚ] log c from deg^ (arithmetic-degree's rescaling API).
Substitute c = π^{−g} (Deligne), c = 2^g (unscaled), c = (2π)^{−g}·2^g relative to unscaled.
acceptance: For g = 1: h_Del(E) = h_Fal(E) + ½ log π ≈ h_Fal + 0.5724; Gaudron–Rémond state h_F(A) = h(A) − (g/2) log π.

nodes.title: The Faltings metric on families and on the Siegel space
nodes.statement: Let S be a complex manifold and A → S a family of complex abelian varieties (proper smooth with abelian fibres) of dimension g. The Faltings metrics on the fibres define a smooth hermitian metric ‖·‖_Fal on the Hodge line ω̄_{A/S}. On the Siegel family X_τ = ℂ^g/(ℤ^g + τℤ^g) over ℍ_g the global frame e = dz_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ dz_g has ‖e‖²_Fal(τ) = det(Im τ), and under γ = (A B; C D) ∈ Sp_{2g}(ℤ) the frame transforms by det(Cτ + D)^{−1} while det Im(γτ) = |det(Cτ + D)|^{−2} det Im τ, so the metric descends to the Hodge line on Γ\ℍ_g and on the complex fibre of the fine moduli space A_{g,n}(ℂ), n ≥ 3. The metric is invariant under complex conjugation of the family.
hypotheses: A → S proper and smooth with abelian fibres (polarizable), S a complex manifold; Γ ⊂ Sp_{2g}(ℤ) the level subgroup.
proofSteps: Smoothness: locally on S choose a holomorphic frame α of ω̄; ∫_{A_s} α ∧ ᾱ is a fibre integral of a smooth form along a proper submersion, hence smooth in s.
Siegel family: covolume-formula gives ‖e‖²(τ) = det Im τ; the automorphy factor of e is A5's det(Cτ + D) convention, and det Im(γτ) = |det(Cτ+D)|^{−2} det Im τ.
Descent to the quotient follows because both sides transform by the same factor; at neat level n ≥ 3 the quotient is the complex fibre of A_{g,n} (PELModuli M3).
acceptance: For g = 1, the Petersson-type metric ‖e‖² = Im τ on weight-one forms; for a modular form f of weight k, ‖f·e^{⊗k}‖² = |f(τ)|²(Im τ)^k is Γ-invariant.

nodes.title: Elliptic curves: the Faltings height from the discriminant and the periods
nodes.statement: Let E be an elliptic curve over a number field K with minimal discriminant ideal Δ_{E/K} (computed from the Néron model at every prime), and for σ ∈ Σ_K choose τ_σ ∈ ℍ with E_σ(ℂ) ≅ ℂ/(ℤ + τ_σℤ). With Mathlib's modular discriminant Δ(τ) = η(τ)^{24} = q∏_{n≥1}(1 − qⁿ)^{24}, q = e^{2πiτ}, the Faltings-normalised degree of the metrized Hodge line satisfies 12·deg^ ω̄̂(E/K) = log N(Δ_{E/K}) − Σ_{σ∈Σ_K} log(|Δ(τ_σ)|·(Im τ_σ)^6) − 12[K:ℚ] log(2π). The archimedean term |Δ(τ)|(Im τ)^6 is SL₂(ℤ)-invariant, so it does not depend on the choice of τ_σ.
hypotheses: E/K any elliptic curve (semistability not needed for this formula, which computes the Néron-model degree).
Δ(τ) here is the normalised q-product, without the factor (2π)^{12}; the lattice discriminant g_2³ − 27g_3² of ℤ + τℤ is (2π)^{12}Δ(τ).
proofSteps: Choose a Weierstrass equation over K with invariant differential ω and discriminant Δ_ω. At each prime 𝔭, ω = u_𝔭 ω_min with Δ_ω = u_𝔭^{−12}Δ_min, so 12·log #(ω̄_𝒜/O_K ω) = log N(Δ_{E/K}) − Σ_𝔭 v_𝔭(Δ_ω) log N𝔭 = log N(Δ_{E/K}) − log |N_{K/ℚ}(Δ_ω)|.

At σ: the period lattice of ω is Λ = ω_1(ℤ + τ_σℤ); by covolume-formula ‖ω‖²_σ = |ω_1|² Im τ_σ, and σ(Δ_ω) = ω_1^{−12}(2π)^{12}Δ(τ_σ) by homogeneity of the lattice discriminant; hence |σΔ_ω|·‖ω‖_σ^{12} = (2π)^{12}|Δ(τ_σ)|(Im τ_σ)^6.
Sum: 12 deg^ = 12 log #(ω̄/O_K ω) − 12 Σ_σ log ‖ω‖_σ, and Σ_σ log|σΔ_ω| = log|N Δ_ω| cancels.
SL₂(ℤ)-invariance from Δ(γτ) = (cτ + d)^{12}Δ(τ) (ModularForm.discriminant_S_invariant, discriminant_T_invariant) and Im(γτ) = Im τ/|cτ + d|².

nodes.title: The hermitian pairing of Ω(A) with Ω(A^t)
nodes.statement: Let A be a complex abelian variety with dual A^t, uniformized as A^t(ℂ) = H¹(A, O_A)/H¹(A, 2πiℤ). The canonical isomorphisms Ω(A^t)^∨ = Lie(A^t) ≅ H¹(A, O_A) ≅ H^{0,1}(A) = Ω̄(A) give a perfect hermitian pairing Ω(A) × Ω(A^t) → ℂ, functorial in the sense (φ^*α, β) = (α, (φ^t)^*β) for φ : B → A. Its determinant metrizes ω̄(A) ⊗ ω̄(A^t), and for α ∈ det Ω(A), β ∈ det Ω(A^t), ‖α‖²·‖β‖² = ‖α ⊗ β‖², where ‖·‖ on ω̄(A) and ω̄(A^t) is Yuan–Zhang's (2π)^{−g}|∫ α ∧ ᾱ| (equivalently Deligne's).
hypotheses: The dual is normalized with the lattice H¹(A, 2πiℤ); with H¹(A, ℤ) the identity acquires the factor (2π)^{2g}.

The uniformization of A^t is Appell–Humbert's description of Pic⁰(A) as the conjugate-linear dual of V modulo the dual lattice (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A5), rewritten through H¹(A, O_A) ≅ Ω̄(A) and H₁ = Λ, H¹ = Λ^* (A4 realization-conventions).
proofSteps: Sum the pairing and its conjugate to a perfect pairing H¹(A, ℂ) ⊗ H¹(A^t, ℂ) → ℂ, dual to H₁(A, ℤ) ⊗ H₁(A^t, ℤ) → 2πiℤ.
Taking determinants and the Hodge decomposition gives an isomorphism ω(A) ⊗ ω̄(A) ⊗ ω(A^t) ⊗ ω̄(A^t) ≅ ℂ dual to det H_{2g}(A, ℤ) ⊗ det H_{2g}(A^t, ℤ) → (2πi)^{2g}ℤ.
Evaluate on generators e_A, e_{A^t} with (e_A, e_{A^t}) = (2πi)^{2g}: the (2π)^{−2g} factors of the two norms combine to ‖α ⊗ β‖².
acceptance: For an elliptic curve E = A = A^t with the canonical principal polarization, ‖α‖⁴ = ‖α ⊗ α‖² for the self-pairing.

nodes.title: The Faltings height of an abelian variety over a number field
nodes.statement: For an abelian variety A of dimension g over a number field K with Néron model 𝒜 over O_K, the (relative, Faltings-normalised) Faltings height is h(A/K) = deg^ ω̄̂(A/K)/[K:ℚ], the normalised Arakelov degree of the metrized Hodge line. For a smooth model G over O_K with generic fibre A (for instance a semi-abelian model) put h(G) = deg^ ω̄̂(G)/[K:ℚ]. nodes.statement: (a) If A has semistable reduction everywhere and G is any semi-abelian scheme over O_K with generic fibre A, then G ≅ 𝒜⁰ canonically, so h(G) = h(A/K). nodes.title: The stable Faltings height
nodes.statement: For an abelian variety A over a number field K choose a finite extension L/K over which A has semistable reduction at every prime (one exists: L = K(A[12]) works, since full level 3 forces semistability away from 3 and full level 4 away from 2). nodes.title: The different of an isogeny of Néron models
nodes.statement: Let u_K : A → B be an isogeny of abelian varieties over a number field K, of degree d, and u : 𝒜 → ℬ its extension to Néron models over O_K (Néron mapping property). Then Lie(u) : Lie(𝒜) → Lie(ℬ) is injective and u^* : ω̄_ℬ → ω̄_𝒜 is an injection of invertible O_K-modules; its cokernel is O_K/𝔡_u for a nonzero ideal 𝔡_u, the different of u, generated locally by det Lie(u) in bases. 𝔡_u is supported at the primes where u is not étale, hence at primes dividing d. If u restricted to identity components is surjective (fppf), with kernel ℳ, then ω̄_𝒜 ⊗ ω̄_ℬ^{−1} is the pullback along the unit section of the relative dualizing sheaf of ℳ; when the finite part M of the quasi-finite flat ℳ is finite flat (in particular when A is semistable, by the semi-abelian kernel computation), 𝔡_u is the classical different of the finite O_K-algebra of M and #(O_K/𝔡_u) = #e^*Ω¹_{M/O_K}.
hypotheses: u_K an isogeny over K; Néron models over the Dedekind base O_K (R11.1).
The comparison with e^*Ω¹ of the kernel needs the kernel to be flat; for non-semistable A multiplication by p need not even be flat on Néron models.
proofSteps: u_K étale on the generic fibre, so Lie(u) is injective and ω̄_ℬ → ω̄_𝒜 is injective; define 𝔡_u as the annihilator (equivalently Fitting ideal) of the cokernel; locally it is generated by det Lie(u).
Where u is étale on identity components the cokernel vanishes; u is étale at primes not dividing d.

Semistable case: the isogeny extends to the semi-abelian identity components (homomorphism extension over the normal base O_K); it is quasi-finite (fibrewise an isogeny of semi-abelian varieties) between schemes smooth over the regular base, hence flat by the fibrewise flatness criterion, with quasi-finite flat kernel (Faltings §4, p. 357).

In the flat case, ω_ℳ := e^*(relative dualizing sheaf) of the lci kernel computes ω̄_𝒜 ⊗ ω̄_ℬ^{−1}; localizing and completing at each prime 𝔭 of O_K, the Fitting ideal of e^*Ω¹ of the finite part is the different of its algebra (FiniteFlat R07.1 invariant-differentials-and-absolute-different at primes of mixed characteristic; at primes not dividing d the kernel is étale and contributes nothing).

nodes.title: Heights along a tower of p-divisible subgroups
nodes.statement: Let A be an abelian variety with semistable reduction over a number field K, ℓ a prime, and G ⊂ A[ℓ^∞] a K-rational ℓ-divisible subgroup of height h_G such that, for every prime v of K over ℓ, the schematic closure of G in the ℓ-divisible group of the semi-abelian model over O_{K_v} is an ℓ-divisible group Γ_v of dimension d_v. Put G_n = G[ℓ^n] and A_n = A/G_n. Then e^*Ω¹ of the closure of G_n has length n·e_v·d_v over O_{K_v} at v | ℓ and vanishes at v ∤ ℓ, so h(A_n) = h(A) + n·log ℓ·(h_G/2 − (1/[K:ℚ]) Σ_{v|ℓ} [K_v:ℚ_ℓ]·d_v). Without the ℓ-divisibility hypothesis on the closures, the formula holds for n ≥ n_0 after replacing A by A_{n_0} (the closures become ℓ-divisible after a shift).
hypotheses: A semistable over K; G an ℓ-divisible subgroup over K; the closure hypothesis at the primes over ℓ.
The global determinant argument that evaluates Σ_v [K_v:ℚ_ℓ] d_v (through Hodge–Tate weights) is FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems R28.2; this node supplies only the local terms.
proofSteps: The kernel of A → A_n on semi-abelian models is the closure 𝒢_n of G_n, quasi-finite flat; at v ∤ ℓ it is étale so it contributes nothing.
At v | ℓ, 𝒢_n = Γ_v[ℓ^n] and length ω_{Γ_v[ℓ^n]} = n e_v d_v (FiniteFlat R07.1 invariant-differentials-and-absolute-different); log #e^*Ω¹ = Σ_{v|ℓ} n e_v d_v f_v log ℓ = n log ℓ Σ_v [K_v:ℚ_ℓ] d_v.

nodes.title: τ-components of the Hodge line under an O_E-action
nodes.statement: Let E be a number field acting on an abelian variety A over a number field K ⊇ the normal closure of E, through O_E → End(𝒜) on the semi-abelian identity component 𝒜 of the Néron model (A semistable), with the dual action γ ↦ γ^t on A^t. For an embedding τ : E → K let W(𝒜, τ) = Ω(𝒜) ⊗_{O_K ⊗ O_E, 1⊗τ} O_K, and N(𝒜, τ) = det W(𝒜, τ) ⊗ det W(𝒜^t, τ^c), where c is the CM involution of E (trivial if E is totally real). At each complex embedding, the perfect hermitian pairing Ω(A_σ) × Ω(A^t_σ) → ℂ (pairing-metric) is an orthogonal sum of pairings between W(A_σ, τ) and W(A^t_σ, τ^c), which metrizes N(𝒜, τ). The τ-part of the Faltings height is h(A, τ) = deg^ N̄(𝒜, τ)/(2[K:ℚ]) (in Yuan–Zhang's (2π)^{−g} normalisation of pairing-metric).
hypotheses: A semistable over K with O_E ⊂ End(A); K contains the Galois closure of E; E is totally real or CM when the CM involution is used.
W(𝒜, τ) need not be locally free at primes ramified in E; its determinant is then taken of the torsion-free quotient, and isogeny comparisons assume local freeness.
proofSteps: The O_E-action on A extends to the Néron model, hence to its identity component, by the Néron mapping property; the dual action on A^t is γ ↦ γ^t.
Ω(A) ⊗ K decomposes under E ⊗ K = ∏_τ K into the eigenquotients W(A, τ); integrally W(𝒜, τ) is the τ-quotient.
pairing-metric's pairing is E-equivariant (γ on A pairs with γ^t on A^t), so it pairs W(A, τ) with W(A^t, τ^c) and is an orthogonal sum.
Determinants give the hermitian line bundle N̄(𝒜, τ); its degree defines h(A, τ).
acceptance: Σ_τ deg^ N̄(𝒜, τ) differs from deg^ ω̄̂(A) + deg^ ω̄̂(A^t) by the discriminant-type correction of the τ-decomposition, which vanishes when all W(𝒜, τ) are locally free and O_K ⊗ O_E → ∏ O_K is an isomorphism at every prime.

nodes.title: τ-component heights along O_E-isogenies
nodes.statement: In the setting of component-line-height, let f : 𝒳 → 𝒴 be an O_E-linear isogeny of abelian schemes over O_K (good reduction) with dual f^t : 𝒴^t → 𝒳^t. Assume the τ-quotients of Ω(𝒳), Ω(𝒴) and the τ^c-quotients of Ω(𝒳^t), Ω(𝒴^t) are locally free O_K-modules. Then the archimedean parts of the comparison map N̄(𝒴, τ) → N̄(𝒳, τ) are isometries and h(X, τ) − h(Y, τ) = (1/(2[K:ℚ]))·(log #coker(f^* : W(𝒴, τ) → W(𝒳, τ)) − log #coker(f^{t*} : W(𝒳^t, τ^c) → W(𝒴^t, τ^c))). In particular h(X, τ) = h(Y, τ) whenever, at every finite place, the τ-length of Ω(ker f) equals the τ^c-length of Ω(ker f^t) = Ω((ker f)^D); this holds when ker f is O_E-isomorphic to its Cartier dual with conjugation-invariant O_E-action.
hypotheses: Local freeness of the four τ-quotients is a hypothesis: at primes ramified in E (or F) the raw quotients can have torsion, and the length count must then be redone with a determinant convention.
proofSteps: f^* and f^{t*} induce a rational map φ = det f^* ⊗ (det f^{t*})^{−1} : N(𝒴, τ) → N(𝒳, τ).
Archimedean: the pairing of pairing-metric is functorial ((φ^*α, β) = (α, φ^{t*}β)), so φ is an isometry at every complex embedding.
Finite: under local freeness the cokernel of det f^* on W(·, τ) has the length of the cokernel of f^*, and likewise for f^{t*}; the degree difference is the difference of logarithms of the orders.
Self-dual kernels: ker f^t ≅ (ker f)^D O_E-linearly (A3 dual-isogeny-and-cartier-kernel), and the τ- and τ^c-lengths match under the hypotheses.
acceptance: For E = ℚ the formula reduces to the difference of the isogeny formulas for f and f^t, consistent with dual-isogeny-differents.

nodes.title: Hermitian metrics with logarithmic singularities
nodes.statement: Let X̄ be a compact complex analytic variety, Z ⊂ X̄ a closed analytic subvariety and U = X̄ ∖ Z, and let L be a holomorphic line bundle on X̄ with a continuous hermitian metric ‖·‖ on L|_U. The metric has logarithmic singularities along Z if every z ∈ Z has a neighbourhood N, a local generator s of L on N and local generators f_1, …, f_t of the ideal of Z on N, with constants C, n > 0, such that for x ∈ N ∖ Z: max(‖s(x)‖, ‖s(x)‖^{−1}) ≤ C·(1 + |log max_i |f_i(x)||)^n. Equivalently (Deligne) ‖·‖ is bounded above and below by ‖·‖₀·ρ^{±r} for a continuous metric ‖·‖₀ on L over X̄ and a logarithmic distance function ρ ≍ −log Σ|f_i|² to Z. The condition does not depend on the choice of compactification, is preserved under pullback, and can be checked after a proper birational modification (Faltings–Chai Remark 4.3).
hypotheses: X̄ compact (the analytification of a proper ℂ-scheme, ComplexComparisonPartII C0); the bound is local near Z only.
Metrics are F_∞-invariant when X̄ comes from a scheme over ℝ or ℚ.
proofSteps: The two formulations agree because log Σ|f_i|² and log max|f_i| differ by a bounded amount and any two continuous metrics on L over compact X̄ have bounded ratio.
Independence of the generators f_i: two systems of generators satisfy |f′| ≤ C|f|^a and conversely, so the logarithms are comparable.

Pullback: along g : Ȳ → X̄ with g^{−1}(Z) ⊂ Z′, local equations pull back to functions vanishing on g^{−1}(Z), and log of a holomorphic function vanishing on a subvariety is dominated by log of its ideal generators (Łojasiewicz).
Birational check: for a proper modification π : X̃ → X̄ isomorphic over U the sup over fibres is controlled (Faltings–Chai leave this as an exercise; Faltings states it with a resolution Φ).
acceptance: The metric ‖dz‖² = Im τ on the Hodge line over the j-line near the cusp q = 0: Im τ = −(1/2π) log|q|, so it has logarithmic singularities along q = 0.

nodes.title: The Faltings metric has logarithmic growth at the boundary
nodes.statement: Let S̄ be a smooth complex variety, D ⊂ S̄ a normal-crossings divisor, and G → S̄ a semi-abelian scheme that is abelian (and polarizable) over S = S̄ ∖ D. Then the Faltings metric on ω̄_G|_S (relative-faltings-metric) has logarithmic singularities along D. In particular, on a smooth toroidal compactification Ā_{g,n} of the fine Siegel moduli space (n ≥ 3) with its universal semi-abelian scheme, and hence (log-singular-metric's modification invariance) on the minimal compactification A*_{g,n} with L = descended ω̄^{⊗m}, the Faltings metric has logarithmic singularities along the boundary.
hypotheses: G semi-abelian over S̄, abelian over S; D a normal-crossings divisor (after resolution).

For the moduli application the toroidal compactification (smooth cone decompositions, so that the boundary is a divisor with smooth relative intersections) and its universal semi-abelian scheme over ℂ are the base change to ℂ of ShimuraCompactifications C4/C5 at neat level n ≥ 3.

For a general (S̄, D, G) the local degeneration structure is not taken from C4/C5 (which are PEL charts); the proof restricts to holomorphic discs meeting D transversally and uses the one-parameter argument of Deligne's Lemme 1.18 together with the bound for several parameters of Faltings–Chai V.4.5.
proofSteps: Reduce to a polydisc near a boundary point with coordinates x_1, …, x_a cutting out D, using the degeneration data: G is the quotient of an extension of an abelian scheme by a torus by a period lattice given by a bilinear form b = ∏ x_j^{s_j} with s_j positive semi-definite.

The squared norm of a local frame of ω̄ is, up to bounded positive factors, the determinant of the matrix of Σ_j −log|x_j|·s_j (covolume-formula with Im of the period matrix ≈ −(1/2π) Σ log|x_j| s_j).
This determinant is bounded below by a positive constant and above by C(−log|x_1⋯x_a|)^g, which is a logarithmic singularity.

One-variable version (Deligne Lemma 1.18): over a punctured disc the lattice Λ_z contains the monodromy-invariant sublattice Λ⁰ extending across 0, and the volume of ℂ^g/Λ_z grows like |log|z||^{2g−r}.

nodes.title: The modular height of a moduli point is m times the stable Faltings height
nodes.statement: Let (A, λ) be a principally polarized abelian variety of dimension g over a number field K and x_A ∈ A_g(K) its moduli point. Then h_{L̄}(x_A) = m·h_st(A), where h_{L̄} is the height of heights-of-points for the metrized modular line bundle (computed on A_g^* over ℤ with the logarithmically singular metric). More precisely, if A has semistable reduction over K with semi-abelian model 𝒢 over O_K, x_A extends to x̄ : Spec O_K → A_g^* through a toroidal compactification and x̄^*L̄ ≅ ω̄̂(𝒢)^{⊗m} isometrically: the two-sided commensurability of the modular line bundle and the Hodge line holds with no correction. For a point y of a fine level-n space A_{g,n} (n ≥ 3) with image x in A_g, the pulled-back metrized line bundle gives the same value: h(y) = h_{L̄}(x) = m·h_st(A_y).
hypotheses: (A, λ) principally polarized; the identity is for the stable height (the relative height h(A/K) can be larger at non-semistable primes).
The integral structure is the one of A_g^* over ℤ of siegel-modular-line-bundle; another projective model changes h_{L̄} by O(1) (heights-of-points).
proofSteps: Extend K so that A is semistable (stable-faltings-height); h_{L̄} is unchanged by field extension (heights-of-points).

The point Spec K → 𝔄_g extends to Spec O_K → Ā_{g,Σ} by properness of the toroidal compactification (C5 valuative-properness); the pulled-back universal semi-abelian scheme is a semi-abelian model of A, hence 𝒢 (uniqueness: C4 homomorphism-extension).
Pull back π^*L ≅ ω̄_G^{⊗m}: x̄^*L ≅ ω̄_𝒢^{⊗m} as O_K-modules (hodge-line-of-group-scheme base change), and the metrics agree at every σ by construction.
Hence deg^ x̄^*L̄ = m·deg^ ω̄̂(𝒢), so h_{L̄}(x_A) = m·h(A/K) = m·h_st(A).

Alternative route without integral compactifications (Faltings 1983 §2, Deligne 1.13–1.17): pass through stable curves and Gabber's lemma to get e·ρ^*M ⊂ ω^{⊗r} ⊂ e^{−1}ρ^*M with a uniform e, which only gives equality up to O(1).

nodes.title: The theta height of a principally polarized abelian variety
nodes.statement: Let (A, L) be a principally polarized abelian variety of dimension g over ℚ̄, with L symmetric and ample, and let r ≥ 2 be even. A theta structure of level r on L^{⊗r²} (an isomorphism of the theta group of L^{⊗r²} with the standard Heisenberg group of (ℤ/r²ℤ)^g compatible with the symmetric structure, AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A3 theta-group) gives a basis of Γ(A, L^{⊗r²}) and hence an embedding Θ : A → ℙ^{r^{2g}−1}. The theta null point is Θ(0) ∈ ℙ^{r^{2g}−1}(ℚ̄) and the theta height is h_Θ(A, L) = h(Θ(0)), the absolute logarithmic height for the Fubini–Study (ℓ²) metric on O(1), i.e. the normalised Arakelov degree of Θ(0)^*Ō(1)_FS. It depends only on the ℚ̄-isomorphism class of (A, L) (another theta structure changes Θ(0) by the action of a finite group of unitary matrices).
hypotheses: r ≥ 2 even, so L^{⊗r²} is very ample (r² ≥ 4); L symmetric defining the principal polarization.
proofSteps: Mumford's theory: the theta group G(L^{⊗r²}) is a Heisenberg group; a symmetric theta structure gives the basis (ϑ_x) of sections; evaluate at the origin.
Change of theta structure acts on ℙ^{r^{2g}−1} through a finite group preserving the ℓ² norms up to the same scalar at every place, so h(Θ(0)) is unchanged.
The height is the Fubini–Study Arakelov degree of sup-metric-height-comparison, normalised by the degree of the field of definition.

nodes.title: Comparison of theta height and stable Faltings height
nodes.statement: Let (A, L) be a principally polarized abelian variety of dimension g over ℚ̄ with L symmetric, r ≥ 2 even, K a number field of definition and τ_σ ∈ Siegel's fundamental domain with A_σ(ℂ) ≅ ℂ^g/(ℤ^g + τ_σℤ^g). In Deligne's normalisation h_F = h_st,Del: m(r, g) ≤ h_Θ(A, L) − ½h_F(A) − (1/(4[K:ℚ]))Σ_σ log det(Im τ_σ) ≤ M(r, g) with m(r, g) = g(¼ log(4π) − ½ r^{2g} log r) and an explicit M(r, g). Consequently, with h_Θ⁺ = max(h_Θ, 1) and h_F⁺ = max(h_F, 1): |h_Θ(A, L) − ½h_F(A)| ≤ C_1(g, r) log(h_Θ⁺ + 2) and |h_Θ⁺ − ½h_F⁺| ≤ C_2(g, r) log(min(h_Θ⁺, h_F⁺) + 2), with C_1 = 6r^{2g} log(r^{2g}), C_2 = 1000 r^{2g}(log r^{2g})^5. In particular a bound h_st(A) ≤ H gives h_Θ ≤ B/2 + C_2 log(B + 2) with B = max(H, 1).

The bound on Σ_σ |log det Im τ_σ| by C(g) log(max(h_Θ, 1) + 2) is Masser's matrix lemma, made explicit by David–Philippon (Pazuki Remark 1.2).

Combine with the matrix lemma bound on log det Im τ_σ to get Corollary 1.3.
Translate normalisations with normalization-adapter (Pazuki uses (2π)^{−g}i^{g²}).

nodes.title: Zarhin's trick
nodes.statement: Let (A, λ) be a polarized abelian scheme over a scheme S (in particular a polarized abelian variety over a field). Then Z(A) := (A ×_S A^t)^4 carries a principal polarization canonically attached to (A, λ). In particular, for every abelian variety A over a field k, A^4 × (A^t)^4 admits a principal polarization over k.
hypotheses: (A, λ) polarized: λ : A → A^t a polarization (A2); the construction is over the base of A, no field extension.
proofSteps: For a free ℤ-module M of finite rank, A ⊗ M is an abelian scheme (≅ A^{rk M}) with (A ⊗ M)^t ≅ A^t ⊗ M^∨ compatibly with biduality; for a symmetric bilinear form B on M, λ ⊗ B : A ⊗ M → A^t ⊗ M^∨ is symmetric, a polarization iff B is positive definite, of degree d^{2 rk M}·|det B|^{2g} where d = deg λ (Moret-Bailly IX 1.2–1.3).

If B is divisible by a suitable power of d, the subgroup K ⊗ M (K = ker λ, killed by d) is isotropic for the Weil pairing of the kernel of λ ⊗ B (polarized Weil pairing and Cartier duality of kernels, A3).

Take M = ℍ ⊕ ℍ for the Lipschitz quaternions ℍ = ℤ⟨1, i, j, k⟩ (rank 4 + 4) and B the real part of the ℍ-hermitian form with matrix (a, b; b̄, c), with integers a, c > 0, c divisible by the power of d required for isotropy on {0} × ℍ, and b ∈ ℍ with N(b) = ac − 1 (Lagrange's four squares); then B is positive definite with det B = (ac − N(b))^4 = 1 and K′ = {0} × (K ⊗ ℍ) is isotropic.

Descend the homomorphism, not a line bundle: for an isotropic finite flat K′ ⊂ ker(λ ⊗ B), the symmetric homomorphism λ ⊗ B factors as π^t ∘ μ ∘ π through π : A ⊗ M → (A ⊗ M)/K′ with μ symmetric (Cartier duality of kernels, A3); μ is a polarization because this is checked on geometric fibres, where it is the descent of an ample bundle along an isotropic subgroup (A2 principal-quotient-and-spreading over algebraically closed fields); deg μ = (det B)^{2g} = 1.
The quotient (A ⊗ M)/K′ is isomorphic to A^4 × (A/K)^4 = A^4 × (A^t)^4, and every choice is made over ℤ, so the construction is canonical and commutes with base change.
acceptance: For an elliptic curve E with its principal polarization, Z(E) = E^8 with a principal polarization (not the product one in general).

nodes.title: A lower bound for the stable Faltings height
nodes.statement: For every g ≥ 1 there is c(g) ∈ ℝ, linear in g, such that h_st(A) ≥ c(g) for every abelian variety A of dimension g over ℚ̄. In Deligne's normalisation Bost's bound is h_st,Del(A) ≥ −(g/2) log(2π); in Faltings' normalisation h_st,Fal(A) ≥ −(g/2) log(2π²) > −3g/2.
hypotheses: Any abelian variety (no polarization needed, through Zarhin's trick).

The sharp constant −(g/2) log(2π) is Bost's theorem, whose primary source (Bost's 1996 Duke article and conference report) is not freely available; the existence of c(g) and an effective non-sharp c(g) are proved from freely available sources.
proofSteps: Principally polarized case: moduli-height-northcott (i) gives c′(g) with h_st ≥ c′(g).
General case: zarhin-height-identity gives h_st(A) = h_st(Z(A))/8 ≥ c′(8g)/8.
Effective form: Bost's Appendix C bounds h_F from below through second-order theta constants (Proposition C.2 and the reduction theory estimates), then Zarhin and duality invariance.
Normalisation translation: normalization-adapter (h_Fal = h_Del − (g/2) log π).
acceptance: For g = 1 the minimum of h_st,Del over elliptic curves is attained at j = 0 (Deligne Remarque 1.5), about −0.749, which is above −½ log(2π) ≈ −0.919.

nodes.title: The height inputs to Faltings' finiteness theorems
nodes.statement: For a number field K and g ≥ 1 the following package is exported to FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems: (a) the stable and relative Faltings heights with h(A/K) ≥ h_st(A) ≥ c(g); (b) for every t, the set of moduli points (in A_g or A_{g,n}) of principally polarized varieties of dimension g over fields of degree ≤ D with h_st ≤ t is finite, with all field degrees bounded by field-degree-constants; (c) the bad primes of polarized varieties of bounded height lie in a finite set depending on (K, g, n, t); (d) h(A × B) = h(A) + h(B), h(A^t) = h(A), h_st(Z(A)) = 8h_st(A); (e) the isogeny formula and bounds of R35.4. The arithmetic bound for all abelian varieties in an isogeny class, the descent from moduli points to K-isomorphism classes, and the finiteness of K-forms remain theorems of R28.

gaps.title: G1: Bost's sharp lower bound for the Faltings height

The existence of a constant c(g) (Faltings–Chai V.4.6, Deligne 1.21–1.22) and an effective constant (Bost Bourbaki 795 Appendice C, Pazuki Remark 1.4) are planned; the sharp value is recorded but not decomposed.

gaps.title: G2: Silverman's formulas for elliptic curves
